ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: the only off-route segment is covered by a rider message that names a road the record cannot tie to the driven path; confirm which road was driven (driver/vehicle telematics, path-name match) before releasing or refusing the metered mileage refund of up to $6.66 [F4][F7]. Check with the rider why she now doubts the road, and note her complaint wording contains no abuse.
ruling.reasoning:
One off-route segment exists, 22:39–22:50, 7.34 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.77 km, +4.57 km, up to 1507 m off the optimal route, and it carries essentially the whole +4.8 km excess [F3][F1][RD-1]. It is not excused by traffic: no incident is recorded near the route in the window, so RD-4(a) is unavailable and the Pan Island Expressway band 2 alone is corroboration only, never a standalone exemption [F12][F15][RD-4].

The only possible excuse left is rider consent. The rider's own message at 22:36, "Can lah, go ahead", answering the driver's 22:35 question, was sent before the segment started at 22:39, and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F8][F9][F10][F3][RD-5]. So consent exists; the dispute is its reach.

The driver's question was "ok if I go round via Bukit Timah Road?" — that is a specific named-road authorisation, not a general "whichever way is faster" authorisation [F8][F9][RD-5]. Under RD-5's named-road branch, the record must tie the driven segment to that road. Nothing does: the chat has only those two messages, no traffic fact names Bukit Timah Road, and the fact table carries no road name for the driven path [F10][F12][F13][F14][F15][RD-5]. The driver's own post-trip statement that he turned off via Bukit Timah Road is a statement, not rider consent, and cannot supply the missing tie [F11][RD-5]. Nothing in the record places the segment somewhere else either, so the honest ground is named_road_untied and the finding is undetermined (G13) — the record cannot settle whether the agreed road was the road driven [F3][F8][F9][F11][RD-5].

That undetermined finding changes the amount: if the segment is covered it is exempt and the refund is zero; if not, the RydeTAXI branch refunds the unexempt segment's extra km at this trip's per-km rate, i.e. 4.57 km × $1.4101/km = $6.44 (the fare record states the rate as $34.35 ÷ 24.36 km = $1.4101/km; billed excess $6.66 for 4.72 km) [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. Because a decision either way moves the money and the record does not let me decide it, the case goes to a person; I do not convert the gap into a refund for either side.

No account flag is available: the driver has two disputes in 90 days but zero upheld and no upheld route dispute, so RD-6's precondition is not met, and profile facts could not decide the case in any event [F18][F17][RD-6]. The waiting component ($0.11) and no surge leave the metered distance as the only contested item [F5][F6][F7][FARE-1][RD-2]. Safety: I read the driver's question, the rider's reply and statement, and the complaint — there is no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE escalation ground arises [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's message of 22:36 ("Can lah, go ahead", F9) answering the driver's 22:35 question (F8) is genuine pre-segment rider consent, but the question agreed to a specific named road — "go round via Bukit Timah Road" (F8) — so under RD-5 the agreement covers driving on that road only. The record contains no path-name fact, stop or positioning message tying the 22:39–22:50 segment (F3) to Bukit Timah Road, and nothing places it elsewhere, so the tie is unproven: finding undetermined (G13) [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement naming the road (F11) is a statement, not rider consent (G11), and cannot supply the tie [F11][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: C5 asks that the untied consent be treated as unresolved; I accept that reading (segment finding undetermined) but not its consequence — an undetermined finding on a segment that changes the amount does not yield a computed refund of $6.44, it sends the case to a person [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. The refund ceiling and rate are correctly taken from the fare record [F4][F7][RD-2] but cannot be awarded while the segment's status is unsettled.

C9 cites the driver's 2 disputes in 90 days as showing he is not a first-time respondent, but the profile shows 0 upheld (F18), so RD-6's precondition (an upheld route dispute in the last 90 days) is not met and profile facts cannot decide the case [F18][RD-6].

D2 is right that the rider's own pre-segment message is consent (F8, F9, F10, F3), but consent exists only as wide as its words: the words name one road, so RD-5's named-road branch applies and the record must tie the segment to that road, which it does not [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

D7 is correct that no unpublished add-on is challenged (waiting $0.11, no surge) [F5][F6][F7][FARE-1], but its conclusion that the metered distance component needs no review does not follow: RD-2's RydeTAXI branch refunds the unexempt segment's mileage, and the segment is not yet resolved [F3][F4][RD-2].

Acquiesced except in its framing: RD-6 is indeed not met because the driver has 0 upheld route disputes (F18), so no flag_account is appended; that finding does not dispose of the metered mileage question [F18][RD-6].
